scope: Manual comparison of the 16 remaining interfaces touching aos-2024-v52-i06-p2791, including 18 source members and the distinct response-regression MSPE member from p2851; all frozen domain, norm, sampling and attainment notes retained.

rows.query: Convex functions with simultaneous uniform Lipschitz and absolute bounds on a domain; inspected ConvexOn, LipschitzOnWith and closed real intervals.
rows.result: Convexity on Omega, a single Lipschitz constant L on all pairs in Omega and pointwise values in [-B,B] directly specify the class.
rows.gap: The existing predicates suffice to define this intersection of convexity, global domain Lipschitz regularity and absolute boundedness.

comparisons.D3: Require both |f(x)|<=B for every x in Omega and |f(x)-f(y)|<=L||x-y|| for every pair, with convexity; L and B are positive fixed parameters and the B=L specialization does not identify them in the general class or replace the pointwise bound by an essential bound.

rows.query: Absolutely uniformly bounded convex functions without a Lipschitz restriction; inspected ConvexOn and closed interval membership.
rows.result: The convexity predicate and pointwise range inclusion in [-B,B] give the complete bounded class.
rows.gap: These predicates directly express the bounded convex class without any additional Lipschitz constraint.

comparisons.D5: Use a two-sided absolute bound everywhere on Omega and convexity; Gamma in the entropy theorem is an instance of B, and no uniform slope bound or extension outside Omega is part of the class.

rows.query: Full-dimensional real simplex as convex hull of d+1 affinely independent points and halfspace representation; inspected Affine.Simplex vertices/independence and convexHull, with simplex face infrastructure.
rows.result: Affine.Simplex R (EuclideanSpace R (Fin d)) d supplies d+1 affinely independent vertices, and their real convex hull gives the geometric simplex. The structure itself stores vertices rather than the closed convex region or an explicit halfspace presentation.
rows.gap: The simplex definition is available through its vertices and convex hull, while the stated d+1-halfspace representation still needs its geometric identification proof.

comparisons.D17: Use a d-simplex in R^d, hence full affine dimension d, not merely a probability-weight simplex or a lower-dimensional face; the entropy theorem's disjoint interiors do not require the simplices to partition all of Omega.

rows.query: Local Lebesgue Lp ball in a uniformly bounded convex class; inspected convexity, pointwise bounded values, restricted measure and finite-p seminorm.
rows.result: Intersect the Gamma-bounded convex class with the Lp ball of radius t about the supplied center under Lebesgue measure restricted to Omega. For positive finite p, this agrees with the displayed integral <=t^p formulation.
rows.gap: These operations suffice to define the local class with its full-domain Lebesgue norm and fixed center.

comparisons.D21: For 1<=p<infinity and t>0, keep the integral of |f-f-tilde|^p over all Omega bounded by t^p and f in C^Gamma(Omega); the center is supplied, and the later brackets on a union of simplices do not change this defining full-domain norm to a restricted-union norm.

rows.query: Lp bracketing entropy on a union of simplices; searched bracketing and inspected function order intervals, restricted Lebesgue Lp width and logarithms.
rows.result: Pointwise ordered endpoint functions give brackets and the restricted Lp seminorm measures their width. A minimum-cardinality family covering all restrictions still has to be defined; ordinary metric balls alone are not brackets.
rows.gap: The bracket-cover counting construction remains to be assembled using pointwise endpoint order and unnormalized Lebesgue Lp on the simplex union.

comparisons.D20: The entropy in (43) is the logarithm of a bracketing number measured on Delta_1 union ... union Delta_k, with Lebesgue Lp rather than normalized uniform probability L2; the union need not equal Omega, and this definition does not repair the separately recorded large-epsilon problem in the printed entropy bound.

rows.query: Convex globally L-Lipschitz functions on a domain with unrestricted intercept; inspected convexity and domain Lipschitz predicates.
rows.result: The conjunction of ConvexOn and LipschitzOnWith gives the stated class; neither predicate fixes a value at one point or bounds the vertical offset.
rows.gap: These two predicates directly express the Lipschitz-only convex class.

comparisons.D4: Keep one Lipschitz bound across Omega with convexity and allow arbitrary additive constants; although each continuous function on a compact domain is individually bounded, no common absolute bound B is imposed on this class.

rows.query: Metric entropy from smallest closed-ball cover, internal/external centers and logarithm; inspected both covering-number infima and IsCover's non-strict radius condition.
rows.result: Both existing covering numbers use closed-radius covers, matching the source's specified boundary convention. They differ in whether centers must belong to the class, which the source does not separately settle; extended cardinalities retain a possible infinite cover size.
rows.gap: The entropy is composable after fixing the source-unspecified center convention and preserving infinity when taking the covering-number logarithm.

comparisons.D19: Use log of the minimum number of closed epsilon-balls covering the function class under the supplied metric, not brackets or open balls; identify functions of zero pseudodistance or use a pseudometric representation explicitly, without claiming that the main text selected an internal-center convention.

rows.query: Normalized discrete Lp function distance on finite grid points and its covering number; inspected empirical atomic measures, p-seminorm and closed-radius covering numbers.
rows.result: The Lp seminorm under the uniform empirical measure on Omega intersect S equals the normalized finite p-power sum. Evaluation vectors or a pseudometric quotient support its covering number.
rows.gap: These operations suffice for the discrete metric and entropy once the finite grid intersection, positive n and center convention are supplied.

comparisons.D22: For every 1<=p<infinity, retain (n^-1 sum_{s in Omega intersect S}|f(s)|^p)^(1/p), with n the actual cardinality in the grid setting; it is a seminorm on full functions, not Lebesgue Lp or an unnormalized counting norm, and covering uses the same discrete difference distance.

rows.query: Convex piecewise-affine approximation of squared Euclidean norm with simplex mesh and k-dependent uniform rate; searched piecewise affine approximation and inspected simplex, affine-map, convexity and Lipschitz primitives.
rows.result: The primitives express geometric pieces, affine restrictions and uniform regularity, but do not supply the quantitative mesh and approximation existence theorem in the source passage.
rows.gap: The missing result is the simultaneous simplex-mesh and convex-approximation construction with the stated dimension-only constants, coverage and uniform error rate.

comparisons.D18: Preserve existence for every k>=1 of m<=C_d k simplices, coverage of (1-C_d k^(-1/d))Omega, pairwise intersections contained in facets of both pieces, affinity on each piece, uniform error <=C_d k^(-2/d) from ||x||^2 and membership in C_{C_d}^{C_d}; full coverage is the extra bounded-facet polytope case, and the lemma provides no unique selected approximant or revised small-k dilation convention.

rows.query: Piecewise affine convex functions on a grid partition into slab-defined convex cells; inspected affine maps and equality on sets, convexity and slab inequalities via closed intervals.
rows.result: Cellwise equality to an affine map, finite intersections of slab inequalities and a partition of the sampled grid define the stated class. Global convexity is an additional condition on f, not a consequence of choosing affine pieces.
rows.gap: The class is composable from these predicates after supplying the finite cells and their grid-intersection partition.

comparisons.D16: Use k convex cells, each an intersection of at most h slabs, with f affine on each and globally convex on Omega; only Omega_i intersect S must be disjoint and cover Omega intersect S, so do not demand full-domain disjointness or coverage, impose the normalized-domain inradius on each cell, or equate h slabs with h facets.

rows.query: Independent uniform design points on a full-dimensional compact convex body; inspected IsUniform normalized reference restriction and family independence.
rows.result: The uniform-law predicate with Lebesgue reference measure gives the normalized volume law on Omega, and iIndepFun supplies mutual independence. Positive finite volume follows from the intended full-dimensional compact body assumptions, not from an arbitrary set.
rows.gap: These predicates suffice to state the uniform independent design law on the specified body.

comparisons.D8: All X_i have the same normalized uniform law on Omega and are independent; do not replace this by the later bounded-density design discussion, treat unnormalized volume as a probability measure, or silently add design/noise independence to this design-only definition.

rows.query: Integrated squared function distance under uniform population or fixed empirical measures and response-regression MSPE on evaluation data; inspected nonnegative integration, L2 seminorm and weighted point masses.
rows.result: Each variant is a squared L2 discrepancy under its specified probability measure; empirical cases reduce to normalized sums while the population case integrates over the domain. Training randomness and the evaluation measure remain separate inputs.
rows.gap: The existing squared-integral construction suffices for each variant once its measure, functions and training/evaluation roles are specified.

comparisons.aos-2024-v52-i06-p2791/D9: Integrate (f-g)^2 under the uniform population probability on Omega; the square root gives the corresponding L2 metric on equivalence classes, and this is not the random empirical loss conditioned on a realized sample in proof arguments.
comparisons.aos-2024-v52-i06-p2791/D11: Use the nonrandom empirical law of the fixed X_1,...,X_n to get n^-1 sum_i(f(X_i)-g(X_i))^2, without adding a regular-grid condition to this formula; distinct full functions can have zero discrepancy when their evaluation vectors agree.
comparisons.aos-2024-v52-i06-p2851/D15: Average (m_P(Z_i)-m-hat(Z_i))^2 on the D1 evaluation observations, with n the size of that split; m-hat is the response regression trained on D1 in Algorithm 1 and D4 in Algorithm 2, so the shared squared-loss formula does not imply an independent test set, the projection-regression training role, or equality with uniform population L2.

rows.query: Expected localized Gaussian supremum minus a quadratic radius penalty under deterministic design; inspected independent Gaussian products, expectation, bounded supremum and convex sets of functions.
rows.result: The Gaussian product law and localized evaluation-vector ball define the random linear supremum, followed by expectation and subtraction of t^2/2. Its measurability, finiteness and concavity require arguments beyond simply writing a supremum and a totalized real integral.
rows.gap: The localized Gaussian objective still needs its supremum and expectation justified and the source's concavity property established for the supplied convex function class.

comparisons.D23: For fixed f in F and deterministic design, localize g in F by the unsquared empirical distance <=t, take the supremum of n^-1 sum_i xi_i(g(X_i)-f(X_i)), then expectation over iid Gaussian errors and subtract t^2/2; F is convex as a set of functions and need not consist of convex functions, and the conditional random-design counterpart is a distinct formula.

rows.query: Maximizing nonnegative radius of the localized Gaussian objective; inspected IsMaxOn and nonnegative real domain predicates.
rows.result: A nonnegative radius and the IsMaxOn comparison over all nonnegative radii express argmax membership. Existence and uniqueness are separate results about H_f, not fields of the generic predicate.
rows.gap: The argmax relation is available once H_f is supplied, while its asserted existence and unique maximizing radius require the source theorem's mathematical argument.

comparisons.D24: Maximize H_f(t,F) over t>=0, including zero; t_f is a scalar radius, not the fitted regression function, so uniqueness of this maximizer does not establish existence, measurable selection or off-design uniqueness of a least-squares minimizer over an arbitrary convex F.

rows.query: All real affine functions restricted to a convex domain; inspected affine maps, linear-plus-constant structure and equality on a subset.
rows.result: Restrictions of real affine maps from Euclidean space to R represent the comparison class, allowing arbitrary slopes and constants.
rows.gap: These declarations suffice to represent the affine comparison class on the full-dimensional domain.

comparisons.D12: A(Omega) contains every affine function on Omega with no common bound on slope or value; the adjacent fraktur-L constant belongs to the distance-to-affine class and does not restrict the affine maps themselves.

rows.query: Convex functions within an empirical L2 distance of the affine evaluation subspace; inspected affine maps, convexity, Euclidean norm and infimum distance.
rows.result: Map functions to evaluation vectors scaled by 1/sqrt(n), take the nonempty set of affine evaluation vectors and use infDist to encode the unsquared empirical distance. Affine trends remain unrestricted in this set.
rows.gap: These operations suffice to define the class after specifying the design-dependent scaled evaluation map and affine comparison set.

comparisons.D13: Require f_0 convex and inf_{g affine} ell_{P_n}(f_0,g)<=fraktur L, using the unsquared empirical distance; the threshold is neither a Lipschitz constant nor a uniform bound, arbitrary affine additions are allowed, and this truth class does not restrict the separate unrestricted convex estimator class.
